gen-righteous-gf-epunda-sans: Righteous bends every letter like a thin steel rod, with bowls that swell to fill the line. Epunda Sans follows with oversized counters and curves full of daylight, so a long passage goes down without a snag.
gen-righteous-gf-farro: Chunky, playful, loud in the best way. Farro steps in with short ascenders and strokes that never swell or thin, and that restraint is the pair's best trick.
gen-righteous-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lines its letters up like nails on a ruler. Righteous bulges with fun above it, while the tall-waisted monospace below keeps a long passage tidy and unhurried.
gen-righteous-gf-geist-mono: Rounded, bold and a bit cheeky up top, with Righteous filling the line with bowls. Geist Mono sits next to it stiff and code-like.
gen-righteous-gf-genos: Genos reads smoothly, its glyphs pressed close and its midline set high, so nothing snags. Righteous does the loud work with a compass-drawn constancy, while Genos handles the quiet work with a modest, gentle weight gradient in its sans-serif strokes.
gen-righteous-gf-geom: Geom reads lofty and friendly, with a tall lowercase band. Righteous gives it a heading with no stroke contrast at all, and that bold uniformity against the plain sans below is what makes the two memorable.
gen-righteous-gf-hammersmith-one: Round, punchy and a bit retro, Righteous fills its bowls to the edge of the line. And Hammersmith One backs it up with rounded strokes like cut cord and capitals barely taller than its lowercase.
gen-righteous-gf-inder: Righteous has a tube-like stroke that looks like neon glass, glowing and confident. Inder settles in beneath with little height difference between its cases, giving the sans a low-key, tidy footing for the heading to shout over.
gen-righteous-gf-jaldi: Approachable from the first line: Righteous bends its neon-tube strokes at constant width, and Jaldi counters with brushed, tall letters. One shouts best; the other talks best.
gen-righteous-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Contemporary and sharp, Righteous looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to one line width. Kdam Thmor Pro is better at quiet, modest text, with softer variation in its sans-serif strokes.
